title: Only 2 Days Of Access To Fable 5 - What Will You Use It On?
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
What Anthropic did was actually kind of funny.

So I got my Fable 5 access back late Thursday. Unfortunately, I was nearing my weekly limit, even  so I couldn't use Fable 5. My limit resets Tomorrow, July 5th at 11pm.

Fable5 is get off subscription and will be api usage only starting July 7th.

So pretty much, I am going to have 1 day (maybe 2 depending the time they make the switch) of Fable 5 to apply to 1 game or related projected.

Hahaha, jokes on me I guess, Anthropic.

The decision of what to use it on is going to tough. What will you spend your Fable 5 access on?

comments.author: account009988
comments.body: “Code me a game that will sell 10 million copies, no bugs, go”

comments.author: No-Trouble-9138
comments.body:
I asked it to create the best web generative roleplaying bot that fits in 20mb... it couldn't because the actual useful models start from 2gb.

I asked it to create the best coding assistant so I can stop paying for it... same story.

So that checks out two in the list.

comments.author: Time_Cat_5212
comments.body: Code me a slideshow app for... Websites ;)

comments.author: Totally_a_Banana
comments.body:
I'm building a game. Its pretty good at coordinating a few of the more complex things I've needed to do, like coordinated enemy and boss design per biome.

It uses coordinated Opus agents (best tip I found to save on usage) but it makes sure everything is cohesive and built well, like a manager running a team of opus agents.

replies.author: Major_Print_905
replies.body: Why have it design the bosses and enemies? Isn’t that part of the fun of creating things? Not hating, genuinely curious

replies.author: AnimalPowers
replies.body:
so, not OP, but creativity comes in different ways.   some people can make things up from nothing. Some people need a seed to start with, and customize from there.   A lump of clay to mold, if you will.   So it sounds like the other person thought “I want lots of different biomes in my game”.  And then told the thing to make them, it’ll get them back and then they will probably think about it for a while and “make the boss be likr this’” and play test it a bit.  

remember every D and D campaign has a dungeon master, but it also has players.   Ant the players, like the dungeon master, help craft the story, just from a different side.

replies.author: Totally_a_Banana
replies.body:
Ive designed a lot, but im not a great artist. Some stuff I pixel art by hand, some are AI placeholders, others I will eventually get to and re-do by hand if I can. But I do need assets and AI can give me a lot of good starting points, like someone else said, and I can iterate and replace from there. But it beats stick figures and blobs everywhere.

In a single afternoon Ive populated 5 biomes, but plan to do a lot of adjusting and replacing from there.

replies.author: NoSociety2178
replies.body: Me too I hope I can get it far enough before the deadline like my own game jam

comments.author: digitalhobbit
comments.body:
I had a game idea for a while. Not quite ready to share any details, but it's sort of a weird mix between god game and sim. I was stuck on some game design ideas to actually make the concept work and (hopefully) be fun, but Fable just helped me push through those blockers. Now I have a solid design. 

Will see if I can knock out the first phase with Fable before it disappears, hopefully get to a playable prototype that validates the concept. From there, I should be able to use Opus for the rest of the work - or worst case, pay for Fable if some tasks really need it.

replies.author: digitalhobbit
replies.body: Definitely an inspiration. Visuals will be more like a colony sim (2d, top-down, think Rimworld or Dwarf Fortress), but the way you interact with the world in a god-like manner takes some inspiration from games like Black & White.

replies.author: AnimalPowers
replies.body: Well, you've got 2 days, get the claude plan and get started.   I would start with a fable prompt telling it ot plan, not execute, and go back and forth with you (interview style) to ensure it gets the requirements before it really starts to do any thinking.    Then have it outline the plan, without doing anything, so you can pass those tasks off to the cheaper agents later in the week.   Anyway, times ticking.  I'd love to see your game.  I loved black and white - i haven't tried any of these other games you mention , but the concept is unique

replies.author: digitalhobbit
replies.body: Thanks - that's basically what I've been doing. Will share it here if it goes anywhere.

comments.body: Design your harness or whatever you want to call it.
